prompt.en: Put that many in the bowl, then hand it to Dalia.
prompt.ar: ضَعْ هَذَا العَدَدَ فِي الطَّبَق، ثُمَّ نَاوِلْهُ لِدَالْيَا.

hint1.en: Count them as you put each one in.

hint2.en: Take one back out if you went too far.

model.en: Watch. That is what that many looks like. Now you make one.
model.ar: شَاهِد. هَكَذَا يَبْدُو هَذَا العَدَد. اِصْنَعْ أَنْتَ وَاحِدًا الآن.

success.en: The bowl is exactly right. The first customer is happy.
success.ar: الطَّبَقُ صَحِيحٌ تَمَامًا. أَوَّلُ زَبُونَةٍ سَعِيدَة.

payload._comment: giveN, not countAndPick, and that is the whole reason this activity is here rather than being a second counting scene. 'How many are there?' can be answered by reciting over the objects; 'bring me three' cannot. A child who can count to ten out loud and still hands over a fistful has not yet got cardinality, and this is the only task in the chapter that would notice.
payload._supplyComment: The counter always holds more than the answer. A supply of exactly the right size answers the question for the child — take everything, hand it over — which is the classic way a give-N task is defeated by accident.

prompt.en: She asked for three apples. Put three in the bowl.
prompt.ar: طَلَبَتْ ثَلَاثَ تُفَّاحَات. ضَعْ ثَلَاثًا فِي الطَّبَق.

revealLine.en: Three apples. Just what she asked for.
Two bananas. The bowl is nearly done.

prompt.en: Last of all, four bunches of grapes.

revealLine.en: Four bunches. That is the whole bowl.
